content: In a second pilot, we investigated the option to take the questions collected for one text and show them as questions for another text of the same scenario. While this method resulted in a larger number of questions that required inference, we found the majority of questions to not make sense at all when paired with another text. Many questions were specific to a text (and not to a scenario), requiring details that could not be answered from other texts. Since the two previous pilot setups resulted in questions that centered around the texts themselves, we decided for a third pilot to not show workers any specific texts at all. Instead, we asked for questions that centered around a specific script scenario (e.g. eating in a restaurant). We found this mode of collection to result in questions that have the right level of specificity for our purposes: namely, questions that are related to a scenario and that can be answered from different texts (about that scenario), but for which a text does not need to provide the answer explicitly.
